meta.title: The Rabbit, the Fox, and the Pepper
meta.textType: story: a traditional story with repeated lines

paragraphs: It was raining in Green Hill, and Lily sat next to Grandma. The room was warm, and the lamp was yellow. Pip lay on the floor next to them. "Can you tell me a story, Grandma?" asked Lily. Grandma smiled and moved her hands in the air. "This story is about a rabbit and a fox," she said. "Say the words with me, and move your hands like me."

A little rabbit lived near a river. One day, she made pasta with a red sauce. She mixed the pasta and the sauce in a big bowl with two long chopsticks. The pasta smelled very good. "Mix, mix, mix the sauce," she sang. "A little pepper, not too much!" Grandma moved her hand in a big circle, and Lily did the same.

A fox came through the trees. "That smells good," said the fox. "Can I have some pasta?" "Not yet," said the rabbit. "First, mix the sauce with me." The fox took the chopsticks, and they sang together. "Mix, mix, mix the sauce!" "A little pepper, not too much!" But the fox put in a lot of pepper. "Ah-choo!" said the fox, and his nose went red.

The rabbit laughed and gave him a glass of water. "I hope you are not angry," she said. "No," said the fox, "but I am sorry." "Mix, mix, mix the sauce," they sang. "A little pepper, not too much!" This time, the fox put in only a little pepper. They ate the pasta together by the river. It was the best pasta in the forest. Pip said, "Ah-choo!" on the floor, and Grandma and Lily laughed. Lily moved her hands one more time and sang the words again.
